gates.evidence: All six native RGBA cell hashes differ. Manual review shows backward/downward head changes in frames0–3, raised attached shoulder feathers particularly frame2, and different forward-profile neck/head silhouettes in frames4–5. This is visible drawing change; distinct hashes alone are not proof of animation quality.

Frames0–3 show a closed or mostly closed bill reaching into the own upper near-wing/scapular feather region. Frame0 already appears to touch feathers, so the intended separate approach phase is missing. A complete nibble/stroke trajectory is not established from stills.

Warm brown/cream streaked female palette, conical bill, folded patterned wing, long tail and two pink legs remain recognizable. No obvious added limb or male-red patch is visible. Feather texture is smooth/fine-rendered rather than strongly pixel-defined; head/neck proportions change between poses. Exact toe count and anatomical correctness remain unaccepted.

Alpha>=128 full-silhouette width is419–428 native cell pixels versus238 in the unchanged half-size reference:1.7605–1.7983 times reference. This is a silhouette scale proxy, not the exact lower-body-width target; visual inspection independently confirms large body/wing/tail enlargement.

Alpha>=128 lowest pixel y506 in each top-row cell and442 in each bottom-row cell; reference lowest y399. A64 native-pixel row-transition jump is visible in feet and lower body. The lowest-pixel statistic is a foot/claw-extent proxy, not an anatomical foot-center measurement. No fixed-root/contact admission is supportable against the4 source-equivalent-pixel target.

Final neutral-return mask IoU with unchanged half-reference is0.2639059261452561 at alpha>=32, far below proposed0.95. Final pose matches broad direction, but scale, feet, head and silhouette do not return to the existing neutral pixels/anchors.

Unregistered adjacent mask IoU drops to0.48087188128499214 across frame2→3 and0.4817435961670946 across frame5→0. Head motion contributes to masks, but the64px feet/body row jump is directly visible. These statistics diagnose registration discontinuity, not perceptual animation scoring.

Native alpha min0/max254,1,101,243 fully transparent pixels, no255 pixels. The brown RGB matte seen by a viewer ignoring transparency is not an opaque background. Proper alpha composite on blue-gray shows no conspicuous brown field/halo at half-sheet review size. Each cell still has8,324–10,033 pixels at alpha1–31, so full-scale contrasting-background edge review remains open; low alpha count alone is not a halo failure.
Local source/prompt/plan hashes recorded. This review does not establish remote storage, playable-clip packaging, PR merge, art acceptance or normal-yard playback.

registeredDiagnosticReview.methodAssessment: All six registered frames independently reconstruct pixel-exactly as a common512→572 nearest-neighbor scale plus documented per-frame integer paste on1024 canvas. No part warping/repainting is detected by this reconstruction. Scale chosen against a neutral silhouette is a diagnostic normalization, and per-frame translation is registration correction. Neither is a new generated drawing or evidence that the model obeyed fixed camera/contacts. Existing raw template failures remain unchanged.
visualFindings: Registered contact sheet removes the obvious top/bottom-row placement jump and broadly aligns the new birds with the old neutral scale. The six actual new head/bill drawings remain visible; this is not registration alone presented as new animation.
Bill-to-own-shoulder contacts remain visible in backward-facing frames. Frame0 already approaches/touches the wing rather than showing an unambiguous separate free approach phase.
Feet now lie near a common baseline, but toe shape/spread and horizontal positions still change. Exact anatomical contact points are not measured by lower-alpha medians.

Body/wing outlines and feather shapes vary; final new neutral has a rounder neck/head profile and different wing/tail/body contour than the old neutral. Uniform placement does not eliminate that identity/shape seam.

The repeated old neutral at both ends creates a trivial identical boundary, while the new neutral-return→old-neutral transition remains visibly different. First/last identity is not transition acceptance.
metricCaveats: quality-review.json field maximumFootDifferenceWithinNewPosesPx=3 measures maximum displacement from the first new pose, not maximum pairwise displacement. Independent maximum pairwise is5px, between poses1 and4 screen-foot1. Both are heuristic pixel metrics, not anatomical tracking.

The lower-body width is silhouette width over fixed y600..719, including changing wing/tail extent, not isolated torso anatomy. It is suitable only for the proposed local diagnostic and cannot prove world calibration.
Alpha128 maskIoU.8567 differs from alpha32 maskIoU.8583 because threshold is explicit; compare like thresholds.
Pixel reconstruction and hashes establish provenance/derivation, not art quality or runtime safety.
registeredDiagnosticReview.recommendation: Keep this as a useful rejected/needs-revision preening source candidate with labeled registered preview. Do not promote neutral reuse, planted contact, art acceptance or species-slice completeness; retain separate storage/PR and normal-yard playback gates.
